headline.text: In Lapin hyvinvointialue, crude curative and life-prolonging treatment shares lag national values, while the crude share with no treatment record within 12 months exceeds the national share.

details.text: The county's crude curative treatment share is 18.5% (95% CI 15.8–21.5; n=131/710) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally, and its crude life-prolonging treatment share is 16.1% (95% CI 13.5–18.9; n=114/710) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence intervals excluding the national values.

Across overlapping treatment categories, the crude symptomatic treatment share is 44.5% (95% CI 40.9–48.2; n=316/710) versus 39.5% (5871/14873) nationally, and the crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 33.8% (95% CI 30.4–37.4; n=240/710) versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence intervals excluding the national values.

The crude share with a recorded multidisciplinary team (MDT) meeting is 3.0% (95% CI 1.9–4.5; n=21/710) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval excluding the national value, though HILMO MDT codes come only from direct patient contacts and measure recording practice rather than care.

Nationally, preliminary, unpublished figures show an average of 155 days from first symptoms to treatment in Finland, compared with 107 in Sweden and 67 in Denmark, including 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care.

headline.text: County treatment shares are crude and unadjusted for age or stage, and the elevated crude share with no treatment record suggests low treatment shares may partly reflect unrecorded care.

details.text: Because the county's crude 33.8% share with no treatment record within 12 months is above the 27.5% national value and mixes untreated patients with unrecorded treatment, we infer as a data-quality signal that the low crude 18.5% curative and 16.1% life-prolonging shares may partly reflect unrecorded treatment.

While national age-adjusted curative treatment shares digitised from a figure (about ±0.5 percentage points) are 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women, the county shares are crude—not adjusted for age or stage—and stage at diagnosis is missing for a large share of new patients.

A journal article found that HILMO diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types, which concerns diagnosis concordance only; Finland has no cancer quality registry, and reporting, collection, and storage of lung cancer data are currently incomplete.

In public data, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned, symptoms and referrals are not measured, and the report tracks whether a specialist visit or treatment type occurred within 12 months rather than when it started.

headline.text: The team recommends publishing recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding, reporting access times using THL guidance 21/2016 definitions, and standardising referrals and diagnostic coordination.

details.text: Given the county's 33.8% crude share with no treatment record within 12 months and 3.0% crude MDT share, the team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding to read gaps as data-quality signals first, while a national quality registry (targeting 90% coverage including stage) and uniform recording instructions are planned.

Because the Health Care Act sets no maximum time for a cancer suspicion and national access-time monitoring is lacking, the team recommends reporting referral-to-treatment access times using THL guidance 21/2016 definitions and flagging stalled handovers while the roadmap plans target access times by 2026–2028 and Filha's diagnostics recommendation is due before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Given the 18.5% crude curative share and the mentor insight that a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating in specialist care, the team recommends a standard referral content list and template, pulmonologist referral for persistent symptoms after a normal X-ray, and a named diagnostic-phase contact while the roadmap plans referral criteria and coordinator guidance by 2026–2028 (adopted by 2029–2031).

q:4e702a20fe.claim_text: Finland has no unified national system to steer the drafting of cancer-specific treatment recommendations, or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care, and cancer-specific and generic PROMs). Existing recommendations and pathways, and the targets and indicators to be monitored, are not coordinated nationally. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
q:4e702a20fe.quote: Suomessa ei ole yhtenäistä kansallista järjestelmää, joka ohjaisi syöpäkohtaisten hoitosuositusten laatimista sekä niihin perustuvien hoitoketjujen toteutusta ja seurantaa (laatu- ja vaikuttavuustavoitteet/indikaattorit, mukaan lukien hoitoonpääsy sekä syöpäkohtaiset ja geneeriset PROM-vointimittarit). Olemassa olevia hoitosuosituksia ja -ketjuja sekä seurattavia tavoitteita ja indikaattoreita ei koordinoida kansallisella tasolla. Tämä ylläpitää alueellista eriarvoisuutta syövän hoidon saatavuudessa ja vaikuttavuudessa.
q:4e702a20fe.quote_en: Finland does not have a uniform national system to guide the preparation of cancer-specific clinical guidelines and the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care as well as cancer-specific and generic PROM well-being measures). Existing clinical guidelines and care pathways as well as monitored targets and indicators are not coordinated at the national level. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
rec:3.location: §3. Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding
